title: The Midnight Theft
summary: A priceless artifact vanishes from a locked gallery. The cameras were dead. Only a microphone was listening.
scenario: A valuable artifact disappears from the Riverside Museum at 11:47 PM. Security cameras malfunctioned, but a nearby microphone recorded suspicious sounds. You must discover how the theft happened and identify the responsible suspect.

events.label: Quiet door
events.description: A latch clicks and a door opens softly, far from the microphone.

events.label: Glass breaking
events.description: A large pane of glass shatters inside the east gallery.

events.label: Faint radio chirp
events.description: Three quiet rising tones from a two-way radio, just before the footsteps.

events.label: Running footsteps
events.description: Someone runs across the marble, away from the glass.

events.label: Metal object falling
events.description: A heavy metal tool strikes the floor and rings.

events.label: Vehicle starting
events.description: A small engine turns over outside the loading bay and pulls away.

evidence.name: Alarm Never Triggered
evidence.description: The pedestal alarm contacts are clean. The case was opened while its alarm zone was disarmed from the security system.

evidence.name: Broken Window
evidence.description: The glass lies inside the gallery, not on the pavement. The window was broken from within, so the break-in may have been staged.

evidence.name: Running Footsteps
evidence.description: Long, hard-soled scuffs run from the window toward the staff door, not away from the building. The runner knew exactly where to go.

evidence.name: Dropped Pry Bar
evidence.description: A steel pry bar, unused: its tip is clean. A maintenance tag is stamped "FACILITIES · A.T."

evidence.name: Unlatched Staff Door
evidence.description: The staff door is not fully latched. The badge reader logged no entry tonight, yet the latch plate is warm: someone used an override that doesn't log.

evidence.name: Cameras Switched Off
evidence.description: The terminal shows an admin session at 23:41 that switched the camera feeds off at 23:43 and armed no alarm zone. The microphone feed was left running.

evidence.name: Escape Vehicle
evidence.description: Narrow tyre marks lead from the dock door: a small car, not the contractor's van parked in bay two.

evidence.name: Facilities Radio Chirp
evidence.description: Three rising tones: the check-in chirp of a Facilities two-way radio. Only maintenance staff carry them, and it sounds a few seconds before the running starts.
evidence.lockedHint: Something faint on the recording hasn't been noticed yet. Listen closely and mark what sounds out of place.

suspects.name: Alex Turner
suspects.background: Eight years maintaining the museum's security and climate systems. Has access to the camera control room.
suspects.statement: "I was repairing the HVAC in the basement. I heard glass break upstairs and called security right away."

suspects.name: Morgan Lee
suspects.background: Curator of the east gallery for fifteen years. Personally authorized the artifact's recent insurance appraisal.
suspects.statement: "I left at ten. I was home long before midnight. I only know what the police have told me."

suspects.name: Jordan Mills
suspects.background: Hired for window restoration in the east gallery. Holds a temporary key card and drives a work van.
suspects.statement: "My shift ended at six. I haven't been back to the museum since I handed in my key card."

hotspots.name: Shattered Window
hotspots.inspection: The east window is blown inward. Glass litters the floor inside the gallery, not on the sidewalk outside. Whoever broke it was already on the wrong side, or wanted it to look that way.

hotspots.name: Broken Display Case
hotspots.inspection: One pane of the display case is gone. The velvet cushion is empty and the pedestal alarm contacts are clean, as if the alarm was never triggered.

hotspots.name: Scuff Marks
hotspots.inspection: Long, hard-soled scuff marks run from the window toward the far corner. The stride is wide: this person was sprinting, and did not hesitate over which way to go.

hotspots.name: Dropped Metal Object
hotspots.inspection: A heavy steel pry bar lies on the marble, a fresh chip in the tile beneath it. Dropped hard enough to ring through the whole gallery. A stamped tag on the handle reads FACILITIES · A.T.

hotspots.name: Staff Door
hotspots.inspection: The staff-only door is not fully latched. Its badge reader shows no entry logged tonight, yet the latch plate is warm to the touch.

hotspots.name: Exit Corridor
hotspots.inspection: The service corridor leads to the loading dock. Cold night air is flowing in, and narrow tyre marks lead away from the dock door. The work van in bay two hasn't moved.

hotspots.name: Security Terminal
hotspots.inspection: The recording terminal is still logged in as an administrator. One entry stands out: Gallery Mic 3, 23:47, thirty-six seconds of audio. The camera channels all end at 23:43.

rooms.name: Main Exhibition Gallery
rooms.objective: Examine the empty display case where the artifact was kept. Was the alarm ever triggered?

rooms.name: East Gallery
rooms.objective: Find how the thief got in: the broken window, the scattered glass and the dropped metal object.

rooms.name: Security Room
rooms.objective: Work out why the cameras failed, and who could reach the recording equipment.

rooms.name: Staff Corridor
rooms.objective: Trace the thief's route through the restricted door toward the loading bay.

rooms.name: Loading Bay
rooms.objective: Find how the thief left: the service entrance and the escape vehicle.

objectives.hint: Walk up to the case in the centre of the gallery and press E.
Go through the doorway on the east side of the main gallery.

objectives.text: Find how the thief got in or out
objectives.hint: Look in the East Gallery for broken glass and tracks.
Inspect objects and press Enter to collect them.
The cameras failed. Find out why.
Each audio-related clue adds an event to the timeline (T).
